output.title: Why some errors keep coming back
output.body:
Some errors keep coming back because the feedback loop is too slow.

If a repeated mistake only shows up when a customer complains, or when you do a weekly review, the same issue can run for a while before anyone catches it. That is how a small rule problem turns into a recurring workflow problem.

The practical question is simple: where is the first point where you can check the work before it reaches the customer, the bank, or the next step in the process?

In a small business, that might be invoice entry, order updates, customer-data changes, or lead follow-up. The fix is usually not “more AI.” It is one clear control: a validation rule, a duplicate check, a daily alert, or a human-only approval gate for anything sensitive.

Money movement and other high-risk decisions should stay with a person. AI can help by flagging exceptions or routing work for review. It should not be the approver.

If you want the error to stop repeating, write down one workflow, one error type, and one place where a check can happen earlier. Then measure whether the mistake is caught before it escapes the process. That is the part worth improving first.
